reason: Verified by driving master.html?v=approach&state=owner-editing. At 390x844 the edited item opens at top 996 (viewport 844) and the fixed .b-edit sheet occupies 464-832, leaving a visible band of only 0-464; at 768x1024 the item opens at 1056 with the sheet at 667; at 1024x900 the item opens at 1016 with the sheet at 543. Pressing 'Move a week earlier' moves the item 996->870, 1056->930, 1016->890 - a real 126px move that happens entirely below the fold, so the owner sees the count, date line, readout and gap note update but never sees the one animated thing in the product. There is no scroll handling anywhere in the sources: grep for scrollIntoView/scrollTo/scrollBy/window.scroll across render-b.js, render-core.js, b.css and shell.css returns nothing. At 1280 and 1440 the editor becomes the static rail (b.css:745) and the item sits at 657 in the viewport, so the moment works there - which is exactly what makes the phone and tablet loss a defect rather than a limitation. This is not a gate restatement: interaction-check.mjs asserts scroll and stepper behaviour only at 1440x960 (lines 319, 346, 366) and never asserts that the edited item is on screen at any width. Only slip in the finding is the illustrative aside: scrolling the item to top 200 at 390 and pressing +7 puts it at top 74, not 326 (the item moves up the measure, not down), but its conclusion holds - it lands fully visible above the sheet at 464. Fix as written needs sharpening on two counts: it aims the visibility rule at a width breakpoint rather than at geometry, and animating the page scroll concurrently with the item's own 0.22s top transition at the same delta would hold the item still in the viewport and cancel the very move it is meant to reveal.
sharpenedFix: Keep it in render-b.js and gate it on geometry, not on width - that is what lets it coexist with the round-1 assertion. Define the band once, after paint: bandTop = 16, bandBottom = (the .b-edit element's getComputedStyle().position === 'fixed' ? its getBoundingClientRect().top - 24 : window.innerHeight - 24). The sheet is the only fixed element on the page at 390 (checked), so nothing else needs clearing. Scroll only by the minimum excess needed to bring the item's rect inside [bandTop, bandBottom], and only when it is outside. (1) On opening the editor: run it immediately, before the top transition starts, so the item is already in the band when the first press lands. (2) On a stepper press: measure after the 0.22s transition ends (transitionend on the item's top, with a timeout fallback) and scroll only if the item has left the band - never during the transition, and never by the item's own delta, or the scroll cancels the move it exists to show. A press that keeps the item in the band must not scroll the page under the thumb. Read prefers-reduced-motion in JS and pass behavior 'auto' when it is set; shell.css line 240 sets scroll-behavior: auto !important but an explicit behavior:'smooth' in scrollTo options overrides CSS, so the media query must be checked in code. This does NOT break 'the page keeps its place through the move' (interaction-check.mjs:346/366): that assertion runs at 1440x960 only, where .b-edit is position: static in the rail (b.css:745) and the edited item sits at 657-739 in a 960-tall viewport - inside the band both before and after the press - so the geometry gate makes the scroll a no-op and scrollY stays 0. Gating on geometry rather than on 'below 1280' also keeps that true at any future width where the rail is present. Then extend the gate rather than weaken it: at 390x844 and 768x1024, assert that after opening the editor and after each stepper press the edited item's rect lies inside [16, sheetTop - 24], and keep the 1440 scrollY assertion untouched as the proof that the scroll never fires when it is not needed.
